headline: Thailand Will Propose 39 kg Arsenic Target at Myanmar Talks
deck: New river research adds a quantified negotiating position to Thailand’s earlier chemical-control plans.
body: Thailand will propose cutting the estimated average arsenic crossing the border in the Sai River to about 39 kg a day, from an estimated 143 kg a day, at talks with China and Myanmar on 24 November. [E1][E4]

In its 22 November report, this paper described Thailand preparing chemical export and transit controls for rare-earth mining and a planned 24 November ministerial meeting. The change is a quantified arsenic estimate and proposed negotiating target; the evidence does not establish an order between those measures. [E9][E10]

Researchers said arsenic concentrations exceeded 0.01 milligrams per litre on every day they assessed. Their proposed target allows 27 kg from mining, 8 kg from natural sources and a 4 kg safety margin; they compared river-sample elements with geological records dating to 2008. [E2][E3]

Yodchanan Wongsawat, minister of higher education, science, research and innovation, chaired a 22 November meeting of more than 250 researchers, specialists and partner organisations. China’s ambassador to Thailand and the head of Myanmar’s working group are due to join the talks; Thai officials are scheduled to meet a Thai-Myanmar working group on 25–26 November. [E5][E6][E8] Thailand also said it would block exports to Myanmar of chemicals used in rare-earth mining. [E7]
